record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; code and linked documents were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README describes subtracting a refusal direction from weight matrices and states that the released LLMs no longer decline harmful requests. This is a qualitative weight-edit result relevant to practical removal, but no run results or quantitative evaluation are reported.
record.gate_note: The README says a notebook reproduces the ablation and a script can measure refusal rates, but neither their outputs nor numerical rates are included. It also claims that general capability is mostly retained without reporting a capability measure. No results are reported for the ShadowLogic models that bear on these claim versions.
record.test_reason: The repository applies Arditi et al.'s refusal-direction ablation as a tool to build compromised GPT-OSS 20B artifacts for evaluating security scanners. The README only asserts that the edited models 'no longer decline harmful requests' and retain 'most of its general capability'. It reports no refusal rate, baseline, control or capability measure. It describes its own verification prompt set as 'deliberately small' with a 'known gap'. No measured result bears on any version, so no verdict is given.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The project packages existing public techniques (Arditi et al. refusal-direction ablation; ShadowLogic graph backdoors) into deliberately compromised models so defenders can test scanners. It asserts, without reported measurements, that the ablated GPT-OSS 20B no longer refuses harmful requests while keeping most capability. It explicitly claims no novel attack and frames scanner failure to flag the models as the finding.
record.recipe_differences: The README describes a weight edit that subtracts a refusal direction from selected matrices, rather than specifying the original activation projection across every layer and position. Repository type: research/tool repository; it says a notebook reproduces the ablation, but its results are not included here.
record.problems: The reported outcome is qualitative and has no numerical refusal rates, stated baseline, uncertainty, or control. The README claims general capability is mostly retained but gives no capability evaluation. The referenced notebook and verification script were not available for inspection in this repository-text record.
record.rows_left_out: No additional result rows. The README's general-capability claim is not recorded as a row because it provides no specific capability measure or evaluation result.

untested.parts: No reported refusal rates before or after the edit, no harmful/harmless prompt sets, no capability evaluation; verification script outputs not included.
GPT-OSS 20B reasons before answering, but there are no results on whether the direction behaves differently in reasoning or MoE models.
No direction construction details, addition intervention, or ability measures reported.

missing.what: Refusal-rate output by category from the verification harness, and any before/after numbers in the ablation notebooks (MoE, graph and weight variants).
Possible evaluation results, layer choice or capability notes in the model cards and reproduction docs.

record.verdict_notes: I changed the relation from 'tests'/T2 to 'uses_without_test'/T4: the ablation is used as a tool to make artifacts, and only an unverified claim of success is given. The ShadowLogic vision models are irrelevant to this claim. If notebook or harness outputs with numbers are recovered, re-assess V2 (abliteration of a released MoE model) and possibly V8 (GPT-OSS is a reasoning model). The README mentions graph-level and weight-level ablation notebooks, which could show sensitivity to how the edit is implemented.

versions.untested_parts: No difference-in-means construction, projection across every layer and position, addition intervention, or reported measurement of retained abilities.
No numerical refusal rates, control comparison, or account of how the result was verified; the README does not report results separately by artifact format.
No tests of attacks suppressing the direction or training against its ablation.
No test or argument about affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts.
No measurement separating harmfulness judgment from refusal.
No cross-language, model-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer test.
No comparison of refusal training methods or stages.
